subject: EdgePath dedicated footprint: tokens/sec, SLO fit, and headroom modeling
messages:
From: Alex Perez <alex.perez@edgepath.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgePath Procurement <procure@edgepath.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Dedicated footprint modeling for EdgePath - tokens/sec & SLO fit

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. We're ramping to GA in Q2 and need a Redwood-backed proposal for dedicated capacity sizing tied to our deal team. Attached is a 7‑day token profile sampled from our staging cluster (edgepath_prod_token_profile.csv) and our SOC2 questionnaire for compliance context. High-level asks: 

- Can you run model-specific tokens/sec estimates and map them to p95 latency SLO fit? Our target p95 is <= 350ms for human-facing chat (average response 140 tokens).
- We need a recommended committed slab (GPU count / SKU mapping) plus a burst plan for 3x traffic spikes and a recommended headroom multiplier for safety (we're thinking 2.0–3.0).
- Please include explicit assumptions (batching, KV cache hit rates, quantization options) and an ops playbook for canary + graceful degradation.

Timeline: would appreciate an initial sizing by end-of-day tomorrow (Feb 17 PST) so procurement can start paperwork.

Crowding in procurement on cc — Alex Perez, Head of ML Ops, EdgePath AI.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Ops
EdgePath AI

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated footprint modeling for EdgePath - tokens/sec & SLO fit

Alex — thanks, got the profile and SOC2 doc. We'll run two scenarios (conservative steady-state and aggressive peak/burst) and produce a rows-and-formulas spreadsheet (redwood_throughput_model_v1.xlsx). Initial clarifying Qs to make assumptions explicit: 

1) Model mix: is production primarily streaming chat (token-by-token) or completion-style (batched full responses)? The token profile suggests 60% chat, 40% batch generation. Confirm.
2) Sequence lengths: you noted average 140 tokens per response — do you have the 95th percentile length? If p95 is much higher we'll size differently.
3) Tolerance for fallback: would you accept a quantized Q8 variant for bursts that increases tail latency variance but lowers cost?

Plan: Karthik will run microbenchmarks mapping your token profile to A100/H100 footprints, and Ben/ I will capture commercial commit recommendations and burst policy. Expect a deck + spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.

Monica Patel
Sales Engineer — Dedicated Solutions
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_throughput_model_v1.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated footprint modeling for EdgePath - tokens/sec & SLO fit

Quick bench notes — mapping assumptions and conservative numbers based on the profile: 

Assumptions (baseline):
- Model: Llama3-Chat-medium-ish family (decoder-only) — 1k token context, KV cache enabled.
- Batch policy: continuous batching with 10–20ms aggregation window for steady traffic.
- Cache hit rate: 40% prefix/KV hits (your profile indicates repeated prompts).
- Network + proxy overhead: 10–20ms.

Per-GPU throughput estimates (p95-safe ranges):
- H100-80GB (production tuned kernels, FP16): ~1,100–1,400 tokens/sec per GPU (steady chat with KV caching).
- A100-40GB (FP16): ~650–850 tokens/sec per GPU.
- Quantized Q8 runtimes (LLM-QL8): throughput +25–40% vs FP16 for memory-bound models but expect wider latency variance on tails.

Latency mapping (single request generating avg 140 tokens):
- Single-GPU steady, H100, 1,200 tps estimate: median generation latency ~210ms, p95 ~320–340ms depending on batching window.
- To meet p95 <= 350ms at GA with a 2.5x headroom multiplier for sustained traffic, compute math below:

Sizing sketch (steady target + 2.5x headroom):
- EdgePath stated baseline sustained tokens/sec: ~1,800 tokens/sec (derived from profile window).
- Required sustainable capacity (H100 eq) = 1,800 / 1,200 = 1.5 -> round up -> 2 GPUs to cover baseline.
- With 2.5x headroom for steady growth + safety: 1,800 * 2.5 = 4,500 tokens/sec -> 4,500 / 1,200 = 3.75 -> round up -> 4 H100s committed.
- Burst plan for 3x spikes: peak 1 = 1,800 * 3 = 5,400 tps -> 5,400 / 1,200 = 4.5 -> so fleet should be able to surface 5 H100-equivalent GPUs via autoscale/burst (or 6 A100s equivalent).

Operational notes:
- Canary: start GA on 2 committed GPUs with traffic mirroring and p95 guardrails; promote to full committed slab after week-long sanity run.
- KV cache warmup: recommend warmup window for new model versions (30–60 minutes) and pre-warming for high-traffic routes.
- Fallback: quantized Q8 variant as emergency fallback; define SLO trade-offs in SLA (e.g., p95 up to 420ms during fallback).

I'll include the microbenchmark logs and exact kernel configs in the spreadsheet.

—Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Perez <alex.perez@edgepath.ai>
Cc: EdgePath Procurement <procure@edgepath.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated footprint modeling for EdgePath - tokens/sec & SLO fit

Alex / team — good thread. A few commercial and ops items to lock with the sizing: 

1) Commit recommendation (based on Karthik's H100-equivalent numbers):
   - Recommended committed slab: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (covers steady + 2.5x headroom).
   - Burst buffer: allow autoscale to 6 H100-eq for scheduled marketing events or unexpected spikes (Doc: burst policy + transient pricing).
2) Pricing / contractual asks: include three-month canary discount and 12-month reserved pricing for the 4-GPU slab. We'll prepare a line-item spreadsheet with unit economics and break-even tokens/sec.
3) SLA: propose p95 compute-only target 300ms with end-to-end p95 <= 350ms. During quantized fallback, declare an agreed degraded SLO with explicit duration and notification cadence.
4) Ops playbook: canary gating, rollback triggers (error rate + p95 delta), KV cache invalidation steps, and warmup checklist.

I'll draft the pricing sheet and procurement playbook for your team — Monica, can you add the exact PO cadence and required compliance attachments for procurement to the spreadsheet?

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. The sizing sketch looks reasonable and aligns with our risk appetite. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Procurement wants the formal price + reserved capacity term sheet and the canary timeline. Procurement contact on cc (procure@edgepath.ai).
- We accept the 2.5x headroom approach and want the burst policy: autoscale to 6 H100-eq for up to 4 hours per day with overage pricing.
- Please include the fallback SLO language you mentioned for quantized fallbacks.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to review the final deck and spreadsheet? Prefer 11:00–12:00 PST.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alex
Alex Perez
Head of ML Ops, EdgePath AI
